title: Tanzanian Coconut Rice
community: Swahili coast — Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Wali wa Nazi — long-grain rice cooked in rich coconut milk until every grain is fragrant, creamy, and perfectly separate. The defining rice dish of the Tanzanian Swahili coast and Zanzibar — the foundation of every coastal celebration table.
longDesc: Wali wa Nazi is the rice that defines coastal Tanzanian cooking — every grain perfumed with coconut milk, slightly glossy, and incomparably fragrant. In Zanzibar, no feast is complete without it. The secret is the ratio of coconut milk to water and the absorption method that seals all the fragrance inside.
ingredients: 3 cups long-grain rice — washed until water runs clear
steps: Combine coconut milk, water, salt, and oil in a heavy saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Add washed rice. Stir once. Return to a boil.
Reduce to the lowest possible heat. Cover tightly.
Cook for 18—20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from heat. Rest covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff gently with a fork. Serve.
chefTips: Never lift the lid during cooking — the steam is what cooks the rice evenly.
Thick coconut milk gives a richer result than coconut milk from a carton.
The resting period is essential — it allows the steam to finish cooking the top grains.
commonMistakes: Lifting the lid — steam escapes and rice is undercooked.
Too much coconut milk — makes the rice sticky and dense.
cookingScience: The absorption method traps steam in the covered pot — the rice cooks through both absorbed liquid and steam condensation. Coconut milk fat coats the starch granules, producing the characteristic separate, glossy grains.
sustainabilityTips: Coconut palms line the entire Tanzanian coast — coconut milk is among the most locally sourced ingredients possible.
reheating: Steam briefly or microwave with a damp cloth.
culturalNote: Wali wa Nazi is the rice of celebration, ceremony, and coastal life in Tanzania. In Zanzibar, it is served at every wedding, Eid feast, and important gathering — its fragrance alone signals that something special is happening.
